messages.subject: update for students and mentors
messages.body_plain:
Students:

Right now the R mentor community is commenting on and rating proposals.
  Some of this is invisible to you, some may be public.  As I said in my
prior email, if you receive comments from any R mentor, please try to be
responsive to the questions raised by the mentor, as it will help us
review and rate proposals.

Mentors:

I note that many mentors are not yet on melange, or have been offered
credentials and have not accepted them.  If you or any of your
co-mentors do not have individual melange accounts, and/or are not
connected with the R Project, you need to get them, and soon.

**Per Google rules we cannot accept any project without a mentor**

Per long standing R GSoC policy we will not accept a project without at
least two mentors.  We also have other preferences and more or less
stringent rules, as I've detailed in several other emails.

If you or one of your proposed co-mentors are on melange but cannot see
R's proposals, please contact me or one of the other R program
administrators (Toby or Virgilio), and let us know what your melange
user id is, and we can offer the role of mentor.  You will still need to
accept this role.

Next, you (mentors) will notice that some of the higher scored project
proposals are being tentatively marked as Accept.  *These decisions are
not final!*  We have an impending deadline where we need to notify
Google how many slots we are requesting.  The 'Accept' slider is being
used to help us count.  If a proposal for your project is not so marked,
you probably need to vote, and comment privately on the application, as
you will have seen on some of the higher scored applications.

Per Google policy we cannot discuss accept/reject decisions in public
comments, or with the students in any way.  Please remember this when
making comments.  Public comments are *only* for things that you want
the student to respond to.

Please feel free to contact me with any questions.

Regards,

Brian

--
Brian G. Peterson

IM: bgpbraverock

messages.subject: Will/should the review process continue April 13-24?
messages.subject_clean: Will/should the review process continue April 13-24?
messages.body_plain:
Tomorrow April 13 is the deadline for R-GSoC organization to request the number of slots from Google.  I understand that the existing ratings/reviews on Google Melange is of great in this aspect.

However, what is not clear to me is what happens after April 13?  I see that on April 24 19:00 UTC there is the "IRC #gsoc deduplication meeting" event for "admins" [https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2015/wiki], but should we keep reviewing/giving feedback to applications?

So, basically, when is the deadline for stop reviewing applications?

Thanks,

Henrik
(matrixStats project)

messages.subject: Re: Will/should the review process continue April 13-24?
messages.subject_clean: Will/should the review process continue April 13-24?
messages.body_plain:
On Sun, 2015-04-12 at 13:56 -0700, Henrik Bengtsson wrote:
> Tomorrow April 13 is the deadline for R-GSoC organization to request
> the number of slots from Google.  I understand that the existing
> ratings/reviews on Google Melange is of great in this aspect.
>

As of right now, the R GSoC project is requesting 22-26 slots from
Google.  In prior years, Google has granted R anywhere from half the
number we request to two more slots than our highest number.

> However, what is not clear to me is what happens after April 13?

On Wednesday, 15 April, we will receive our slot allocation from Google.

By Monday, 21 April, we have to have the correct number of projects
marked 'Accept'.

The time between the 15th and the 21st is a critical one, especially for
projects on or near the interface in scoring.  We want all R mentors to
chime in on as many projects as they feel qualified to render an opinion
on.  Projects can and do move up and down in this middle area of the
rankings.  the top projects tend to get higher scores overall, higher
average scores, and more mentors voting for them.  This is expected.

The middle tranche benefits most from (private) discussion amongst the
mentor community. We have often made decisions in the middle group of
projects based on input from the mentor community.

> I see that on April 24 19:00 UTC there is the "IRC #gsoc deduplication
> meeting" event for
> "admins" [https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2015/wiki], but should we
> keep reviewing/giving feedback to applications?
>

See above.

Between April 21 and 24, we hope we have no duplicates.  If we do, then
we adjust.

Between the 24th and the 27th, we wait.

> So, basically, when is the deadline for stop reviewing applications?
>

Effectively, the 21st.

Regards,

Brian

--

messages.subject: R receives 26 slots for GSoC 2015
messages.body_plain:
R GSoC has received 26 project slots from Google, more than any prior
year.

We received 79 student proposals this year.

Between now and the 24th, we need to finalize slot allocations.

Mentors, as I've said in prior emails, your opinion matters, now
especially at the interface near the accept/don't accept boundary, or
where there are two or more proposals for a project (there are many
instances of this).  You should also make sure that you have scored and
commented privately on your preferred proposal for your projects, and
communicate privately with other mentors where appropriate.

Students:  please pay attention to public comments on your proposals.
You may still receive them as we finalize allocations.

Regards,

Brian

--
